source_text: Ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν παιζόντων ἐστὶ, καὶ ταῖς τῶν λόγων στροφαῖς ἐπαγαλλομένων πρὸς τοὺς ἀπείρους· τὸ δὲ ἀληθὲς οὐχ οὕτως ἔχει. Ἄνθρωποι γὰρ λέγονται οἱ τοῖς ἀνθρωπίνοις ἔτι παθήμασι κατεχόμενοι· ὁ δὲ ὑψηλότερος ἤδη τῶν σαρκικῶν παθημάτων γενόμενος, καὶ διὰ τὴν τοῦ νοῦ τελείωσιν πρὸς τὴν τῶν ἀγγέλων κατάστασιν μετελθὼν, οὗτος ὅταν περὶ τῶν ἀν θρωπίνων διαλέγηται, ἑαυτὸν ὑπεξαιρεῖται τῶν λοι πῶν δηλονότι. Ἀψευδὴς γὰρ ὁ εἰπών· Ἐγὼ εἶπα· Θεοί ἐστε, καὶ υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου πάντες· ὑμεῖς δὲ ὡς ἄνθρωποι ἀποθνήσκετε. Θεοί ἐστε. Πάντως δὲ εἴ τινι ἄλλῳ, καὶ τῷ Δαβὶδ ἡ τοιαύτη προσηγορία πρέπουσα. Καὶ γὰρ καὶ υἱὸς Ὑψίστου, ὁ διὰ τῆς ἀρετῆς ᾠκειωμένος Θεῷ, καὶ οὐκ ἀποθνήσκων ὡς ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλὰ ζῶντα ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὸν Θεόν. Ἐγὼ οὖν εἶπον, φησὶν, ἐν τῇ ἐκστάσει μου· Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης. Ἀκουέτωσαν οἱ τῇ μὲν σαρκὶ διὰ τῶν παθημάτων συμπεφυρμένοι, τὸν δὲ νοῦν ἑαυτῶν ὑπεραίροντες τῶν ὑπερκοσμίων· ὧν τοὺς λογισμοὺς καθαιρεῖν, καὶ τὸ ὕψωμα τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν τῆς κατεπαιρομένης τοῦ Θεοῦ, κοινὸς ἔστω σκοπὸς πᾶσι τοῖς ἀντιποιουμένοις τῆς εὐσεβείας. Τί ἀνταποδώσω τῷ Κυρίῳ περὶ πάντων ὧν ἀνταπέδωκέν μοι; Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι. Εἰς αἴσθησιν ἐλθὼν τῶν μυρίων παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ δωρεῶν, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος εἰς τὸ εἶναι παρήχθη· ὅτι ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς διαπλασθεὶς, λόγῳ τετίμηται, ἐν ᾧ καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα φορεῖν δύναται τοῦ ἐπουρανίου· ἔπειτα καὶ πρὸς τὴν ὑπὲρ τοῦ γένους τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἰκονομίαν ἀπιδὼν, ὅτι ἑαυτὸν ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκε λύτρον ἀντὶ πάντων ἡμῶν, ἐπαπορεῖ, καὶ ζητεῖ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτῷ, τί ἄξιον ἐξεύρῃ δῶρον τῷ Δεσπότῃ. Τί οὖν, φησὶν, ἀνταποδώσω τῷ Κυρίῳ; Οὐ θυσίας, οὐδὲ ὁλοκαυτώσεις, οὐδὲ τὴν ἐκ τῆς νομικῆς λατρείας θεραπείαν, ἀλλ' αὐτὴν πᾶσαν τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ ζωήν· καὶ διὰ τοῦτο, φησὶ, Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι, τὸ ἐν τοῖς ἀγῶσι τοῖς ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐσεβείας πάθος, τὸ μέχρι θανάτου πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἀντικατα στῆναι, ποτήριον λέγων. Τοῦτο δ' ἂν εἴη ὅπερ αὐτὸς ἐδίδαξεν ὁ Σωτὴρ ἐν τοῖς Εὐαγγελίοις· Πάτερ, εἰ δυνατὸν, παρελθέτω τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο· καὶ πάλιν τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον, ὃ ἐγὼ μέλλω πίνειν; ἐδήλου δὲ τὸν θάνατον, ὃν κατεδέχετο ὑπὲρ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου σωτηρίας. Διὰ τοῦτο, φησὶ, Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι· τουτέστι, διψῶν ἐπὶ τὴν διὰ τοῦ μαρτυρίου τελείωσιν ἔρχομαι, ἀνάπαυσιν ψυχῆς καὶ σώματος, οὐκ ἀλγηδόνας τιθέμενος τὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐσεβείας ἀγῶσι προσαγόμενα κολαστήρια. Ἐμαυτὸν οὖν, φησὶ, θυσίαν προσοίσω καὶ προσφορὰν τῷ Κυρίῳ, ἐπειδὴ πάντα μικρότερα τί θεμαι τῆς ἀξίας τοῦ εὐεργετήσαντος. Καὶ ταύτας τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἑτοίμως ἔχω ὑπὸ μάρτυρι παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ἀποτῖσαι. Τὰς γὰρ εὐχάς μου ἀποδώσω ἐναντίον παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ. Εἶτα προτροπὴ πρὸς τοὺς ἀκροατὰς ὑπὲρ τοῦ μὴ καταπλαγῆναι τὸν θάνατον. Τίμιος, φησὶν, ἐναντίον Κυρίου, ὁ θάνατος τῶν ὁσίων αὐτοῦ. Μὴ ὀκνήσητε, φησὶ, πρὸς ἀγῶνα τὸν καλὸν, οἱ ἄνθρωποι, μηδὲ ἀποδειλιάσητε πρὸς τὸν θάνατον· οὐ γὰρ φθορά ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ ζωῆς ἀφορ μή· οὐκ ἀφανισμός ἐστι παντελὴς, ἀλλὰ μετάβασις πρὸς τιμήν.
thought_title: True meaning of 'every man is a liar' and the cup of salvation as martyrdom
orientation: Basil has just dismissed the sophistical objection to 'every man is a liar' as wordplay, and now gives the true interpretation before turning to the psalmist's vow of the cup of salvation.
pass_a_gloss: But these things belong to those who jest, and who exult in the twists of words against the inexperienced; but the truth is not so. For 'men' are called those who are still held by human passions; but he who has already become higher than the fleshly passions, and through the perfection of the mind has passed over to the state of the angels, this man, whenever he speaks about human things, exempts himself from the rest, clearly. For he who said is not lying: 'I said: You are gods, and all sons of the Most High; but you die as men.' You are gods. And surely if to any other, to David also such an address is fitting. For he is also a son of the Most High, the one made akin to God through virtue, and not dying as a man, but having the living God in himself. 'I therefore said,' he says, 'in my ecstasy: Every man is a liar.' Let those hear who are mixed together with the flesh through the passions, but who raise their own mind above the things above the world; to tear down the reasonings of these, and the height of their heart that is lifted up against God, let it be a common aim for all who lay claim to piety. 'What shall I give back to the Lord for all that he has given back to me? I will take the cup of salvation.' Having come to perception of the countless gifts from God, that from not being he was brought into being; that having been formed from the earth, he has been honored with reason, in which he is also able to wear the image of the heavenly one; then also having looked to the dispensation for the race of men, that the Lord gave himself as a ransom in place of all of us, he is at a loss, and seeks among all the things that belong to him, what worthy gift he may find for the Master. 'What then,' he says, 'shall I give back to the Lord?' Not sacrifices, nor whole burnt offerings, nor the service from the legal worship, but my whole life itself; and because of this, he says, 'I will take the cup of salvation,' calling the suffering in the contests for the sake of piety, the standing against sin unto death, a cup. And this would be what the Savior himself taught in the Gospels: 'Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass'; and again to the disciples: 'Can you drink the cup which I am about to drink?' and he was indicating the death which he was accepting for the salvation of the world. Because of this, he says, 'I will take the cup of salvation'; that is, thirsting I come to the perfection through martyrdom, setting as rest of soul and body, not pains, the punishments brought on in the contests for the sake of piety. 'Myself therefore,' he says, 'I will offer as a sacrifice and an offering to the Lord, since I consider all things smaller than the worth of the benefactor. And these promises I have ready to pay back before all the people as witness. For I will pay my vows before all his people.' Then an exhortation to the hearers not to be terrified at death. 'Precious,' he says, 'before the Lord, is the death of his holy ones.' Do not shrink, he says, from the good contest, O men, nor be cowardly toward death; for it is not corruption, but a starting point of life; it is not complete destruction, but a passage to honor.

choices.why: Basil dismisses the sophistical objection as play, not serious argument; 'jest' captures the mocking tone.
στροφαῖς means turns or twists; 'twists of words' conveys the verbal trickery Basil condemns.
The verb means to take out from under or remove oneself; 'exempts himself' captures the reflexive removal from the category of 'men.'
Fixed glossary term; rendered exactly as specified.

choices.english: before all the people as witness
choices.why: The dative μάρτυρι with ὑπὸ indicates presence before a witness; 'before all the people as witness' preserves the public, attested character of the vow.
rejected: with all the people as witness
under witness of all the people

choices.english: that is lifted up against God
choices.why: The participle is middle/passive; 'is lifted up' preserves the passive force, indicating the heart's exaltation against God rather than an active reflexive action.
rejected: that lifts itself up against God

pass_b_english: But these are the games of people who jest and delight in the twists of words at the expense of the inexperienced. The truth is not like that. For those are called men who are still held by human passions. But the one who has already risen above the passions of the flesh, and through the perfection of his mind has passed over to the state of the angels—when he speaks about human things, he clearly exempts himself from the rest. For the one who said, “I said, ‘You are gods, and all of you sons of the Most High; but you die like men’” (Psalm 82:6-7, LXX 81:6-7), is truthful. “You are gods.” And certainly if to anyone else, this title is fitting also for David. For he too is a son of the Most High, made akin to God through virtue, and he does not die like a man, but having God living within himself.

“I said in my ecstasy,” he says, “‘Every man is a liar’” (Psalm 116:11, LXX 115:2). Let those hear this who are mixed together with the flesh through their passions, yet exalt their own minds above the things beyond the world. Let it be the common aim of all who lay claim to piety to tear down their reasonings and the height of their heart that is lifted up against God.

“What shall I give back to the Lord for all that he has given back to me? I will take the cup of salvation” (Psalm 116:12-13, LXX 115:3-4). Coming to awareness of the countless gifts from God—that he was brought from non-being into being; that, formed from the earth, he was honored with reason, in which he is also able to bear the image of the heavenly one; and then, looking also to the plan for the human race, that the Lord gave himself as a ransom for us all—he is at a loss, and searches among all that he possesses for what worthy gift he might find for the Master.

“What then,” he says, “shall I give back to the Lord?” Not sacrifices, not whole burnt offerings, not the service of the legal worship, but my whole life itself. And for this reason, he says, “I will take the cup of salvation,” meaning the suffering in the contests for the sake of piety, the standing against sin even to death. And this would be what the Savior himself taught in the Gospels: “Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me” (Matthew 26:39); and again to the disciples, “Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?” (Matthew 20:22). He was indicating the death he accepted for the salvation of the world.

For this reason, he says, “I will take the cup of salvation”—that is, thirsting, I come to the perfection through martyrdom, counting not as pains the tortures brought on in the contests for piety, but as rest for soul and body. “I will offer myself,” he says, “as a sacrifice and offering to the Lord, since I consider all things too small for the worth of my benefactor. And these promises I am ready to pay before all the people, who are my witnesses. For I will pay my vows in the presence of all his people” (Psalm 116:14, LXX 115:5).

Then comes an exhortation to the hearers not to be terrified by death. “Precious before the Lord,” he says, “is the death of his holy ones” (Psalm 116:15, LXX 115:6). Do not shrink from the good contest, you people, and do not be cowardly before death. For it is not corruption, but the starting point of life; it is not utter destruction, but a passage to honor.
notes: The source text contains several line-break hyphenations (ἀν θρωπίνων, λοι πῶν, ἀντικατα στῆναι, τί θεμαι, ἀφορ μή) that appear to be OCR artifacts from the original line breaks; they have been resolved in the gloss.

problems.why: ὑπὸ μάρτυρι means 'before/as witness,' but English makes 'witness' the object of payment, not the context.
problems.fix: before all the people as my witness

problems.quote: And if this title belongs to anyone, it certainly belongs to David.
problems.source_quote: Πάντως δὲ εἴ τινι ἄλλῳ, καὶ τῷ Δαβὶδ ἡ τοιαύτη προσηγορία πρέπουσα.
problems.why: Source says 'if to anyone else, then also to David this title is fitting.' English reverses the emphasis and drops 'else' (ἄλλῳ).
problems.fix: And certainly if to anyone else, this title is fitting also for David.
problems.ruling: ἄλλῳ means 'else'; omission changes meaning from 'if to anyone else' to unconditional 'if to anyone.'

problems.quote: but has the living God within himself
problems.source_quote: ἀλλὰ ζῶντα ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὸν Θεόν
problems.why: Source says 'having God living within himself' (God is the one living inside him), not 'the living God.'
problems.fix: but having God living within himself
problems.ruling: ζῶντα modifies ἔχων, not τὸν Θεόν: 'having God living in himself,' not 'the living God.'

problems.quote: yet raise their own minds above the things beyond the world
problems.source_quote: τὸν δὲ νοῦν ἑαυτῶν ὑπεραίροντες τῶν ὑπερκοσμίων
problems.why: ὑπεραίρειν + genitive means 'exalt themselves above,' not 'raise minds above.' They exalt themselves above the supramundane things.
problems.fix: yet exalt their own minds above the things beyond the world
problems.ruling: ὑπεραίροντες τῶν ὑπερκοσμίων = exalting themselves above supramundane things; 'raise their minds above' misrepresents subject and verb sense.

problems.quote: thirsting, I come to the perfection through martyrdom, counting the torments brought against me in the contests for piety as rest for soul and body, not as pains
problems.source_quote: διψῶν ἐπὶ τὴν διὰ τοῦ μαρτυρίου τελείωσιν ἔρχομαι, ἀνάπαυσιν ψυχῆς καὶ σώματος, οὐκ ἀλγηδόνας τιθέμενος τὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐσεβείας ἀγῶσι προσαγόμενα κολαστήρια
problems.why: Source says 'not setting the punishments as pains,' i.e., he does not regard them as pains. English 'counting...as rest...not as pains' reverses the construction.
problems.fix: not setting as pains the punishments brought on in the contests for piety, but as rest for soul and body
problems.ruling: οὐκ ἀλγηδόνας τιθέμενος = 'not setting/regarding as pains'; English 'counting...not as pains' inverts to active 'counting,' changing construction.
